items.title: 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness
items.description: …Says 13.9m voters in North-East must not be disenfranchised By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has charged electoral officials across the North-East to uphold strict neutrality, strengthen operational preparedness and ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the charge on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections held in Gombe State. He said the credibility of the forthcoming elections would depend largely on the professionalism, integrity, punctuality and preparedness of electoral personnel at polling units, ward collation centres and local government offices. The INEC chairman warned that administrative negligence, logistical failures, partisan conduct and poor communication could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and provide opportunities for the spread of misinformation. According to him, the commission’s nationwide readiness assessment was designed to identify operational gaps, assess the preparedness of personnel and strengthen institutional capacity ahead of the elections. Amupitan explained that the North-East engagement followed similar exercises in the South-West, North-West and South-East geopolitical zones, adding that the commission’s leadership had undertaken physical inspections of electoral facilities in Gombe as part of its efforts to evaluate preparedness on the ground. He disclosed that the leadership had visited the palace of the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, and inspected INEC’s zonal store and Gombe Local Government Area office. He said the inspections were necessary to establish the commission’s actual level of preparedness rather than rely solely on administrative reports from headquarters. “The true integrity of an election is not determined in conference rooms in Abuja; it is forged in the field,” Amupitan said, stressing that the conduct of electoral officials at the grassroots would ultimately shape public perceptions of the 2027 polls. 13.9 million voters in North-East. Highlighting the electoral significance of the North-East, the INEC chairman disclosed that the zone accounted for 13,965,475 registered voters across Bauchi, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba, Gombe and Yobe states. The figure, he said, represented approximately 13.51 per cent of Nigeria’s registered voter population of more than 103 million. A breakdown presented at the meeting showed that Bauchi State had 3,012,547 registered voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. Gombe State, with 11 local government areas, 114 registration areas and 3,311 polling units, was described as an important operational centre for electoral logistics and regional coordination. Amupitan stressed that the figures represented millions of citizens whose constitutional right to choose their leaders must be protected through transparent, secure and efficient electoral administration. He urged officials to eliminate administrative bottlenecks, improve the distribution and collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), and ensure that logistical shortcomings did not prevent eligible Nigerians from participating in the elections. INEC intensifies preparations for 2027. The post 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kozah/consommation locale : les acteurs de l’agroalimentaire sensibilisés sur les dangers du formol et du bromate de potassium
items.description: Kara, 27 oct. (ATOP) – Les producteurs, transformateurs et commerçants de la région de la Kara ont été sensibilisés, le lundi 16 octobre, sur les risques sanitaires liés à l’utilisation du formol et du bromate de potassium dans la transformation et la conservation des produits agroalimentaires. Initiée par la direction régionale du Commerce et du Contrôle de la qualité, en collaboration avec INADES-Formation et la Chambre de métiers, cette rencontre s’inscrit dans le cadre de la 7 e édition du mois du consommer local placée sous le thème « La consommation locale, facteur d’intégration régionale et de souveraineté économique : défis et opportunités ». Cette rencontre vise à renforcer les connaissances des acteurs de la chaîne agroalimentaire sur les dangers de ces substances chimiques, à promouvoir le respect des normes de qualité et de sécurité sanitaire et à encourager la mise sur le marché de produits locaux sains et compétitifs. Les échanges ont porté notamment sur les conséquences sanitaires de l’utilisation du formol et du bromate de potassium, les bonnes pratiques de transformation et de conservation des aliments, ainsi que les exigences de contrôle et de certification des produits locaux. Le préfet de la Kozah, colonel Bonfoh Farè, a souligné que la promotion de la consommation locale doit nécessairement s’accompagner du respect des normes sanitaires, afin de préserver la santé des populations et de renforcer la confiance des consommateurs. Il a relevé que la valorisation des produits locaux constitue un levier de création d’emplois, d’amélioration des revenus et de réduction de la dépendance aux importations. Selon lui, la qualité et la compétitivité des produits togolais représentent également des atouts pour accéder aux marchés régionaux, notamment dans le cadre de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf). La directrice de la Consommation locale, Mme Adovon Mayéka Félicité, a insisté sur la nécessité de concilier la promotion du « Made in Togo » avec les exigences de qualité. Elle a rappelé l’existence de dispositifs nationaux d’analyse, de contrôle et de certification des produits, ainsi que l’obligation faite aux producteurs de soumettre leurs produits aux analyses requises avant leur commercialisation. Mme Adovon a indiqué que les initiatives de promotion de la consommation locale ont contribué à une augmentation de plus de 40 % du chiffre d’affaires des transformateurs, selon les données officielles. Elle a également évoqué la présence croissante des produits togolais dans les grandes surfaces et l’élargissement des réseaux de distribution grâce aux foires et expositions. ATOP/AE/AR

items.title: ATC reserves verdict in security breach case against Imaan, Hadi
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The trial of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, in the security breach case concluded at Adiala Jail on Tuesday, with the anti-terrorism court (ATC) reserving its verdict. Imaan and Hadi are facing a jail trial in a 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on October 7. On Tuesday, both accused recorded their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, while final arguments by the state counsel also concluded during the proceedings. Following the completion of the trial and final arguments, the court reserved its verdict and said that it would be pronounced on October 29. A day prior, the couple approached the Supreme Court to challenge the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case. The IHC had heard their appeals last week against an Oct 10 ATC order dismissing petitions challenging the framing of charges and the inclusion of terrorism-related provisions. The high court issued notices and said it would decide how to proceed after receiving responses from the parties. The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the high court Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

items.title: Average building cost increases by 5.1% in September 2026 -GSS
items.description: The year-on-year inflation rate measured by the Prime Building Cost Index (PBCI) has increased to 5.1 percent in September 2026 from 4.6 percent in August 2026 By this, building costs were 5.1% higher than a year ago and 0.03% higher than in August 2026. Plant and equipment costs went up 19.1% over the year, and were the main pressure point. The monthly change rate for September 2026 was 0.03 percent. In press release, the Ghana Statistical Service explained that the index tracks the prices of key construction inputs such as building materials, labour, and equipment over time, indexed to the 2023 base year, which is set at 100. “In simple terms, the PBCI shows whether it is becoming more expensive or cheaper to build compared to a previous period. PBCI is used by key stakeholders including investors, developers, contractors, and policy makers to negotiate contracts, adjust bids, budget effectively, and monitor inflation trends in the building sector”, it said. At the group level, the Labour group inflation rate recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of -3.2 percent in September 2026 down from -2.9 in August 2026. The Material group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 6.5 percent in September 2026 up from 5.8 percent in August 2026 while the Plant group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 19.1 percent up from 17.9 percent in August 2026. At the sub-group level, Reinforcement recorded the highest year-on-year inflation rate of 29.0 percent while the sub-group Steel recorded the lowest year-on-year inflation rate of -8.8 percent. Fourteen sub-groups out of the 23 sub-groups recorded inflation rate above the national average of 5.1 percent. September 2026 PBCI Bulletin Download

items.title: Gold Fields’ US$4.26bn local spend puts mining value retention in focus
items.description: Gold Fields Ghana Limited has spent US$4.26 billion on goods and services over five years, including US$2.59 billion in its host communities, putting the spotlight on how mining procurement can translate into lasting economic opportunities for local businesses. The company says 93% of its procurement was undertaken in-country over the same period, with almost 100 community vendors involved in its supply chain. It has tracked host community procurement since 2016 as part of efforts to retain and share more of the economic value generated by its operations with communities hosting its mines. The figures underline the scale of mining-related expenditure flowing through the domestic economy. Mining operations generate significant demand for goods and services, much of it channelled through subcontracted operational services. Transport, fuel, power, maintenance, protective equipment and other supplies create opportunities for domestic businesses, although the extent of the wider economic benefit depends on how much value is retained locally. Gold Fields says its commitment to contracting Ghanaian-owned and controlled businesses predates the introduction of Ghana’s current mining local-content regulations. In 2010, the company contracted a wholly Ghanaian-owned fuel supplier, Zen Petroleum, ahead of the introduction of the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2431). It also engaged Genser Energy, a Ghanaian-founded and controlled business, as an independent power producer to supply electricity to its Tarkwa and Damang mines. Western Transport Services Limited (WTS), a Ghanaian-owned company, was contracted to provide transportation services at both sites. These examples illustrate how mining procurement can support Ghanaian businesses in providing essential operational services. They also highlight the importance of examining local procurement beyond the headline expenditure figures, including the ownership of suppliers, the nature of goods and services supplied and the capacity created within the domestic economy. Gold Fields’ procurement record will be among the issues providing context for the company’s Suppliers Conference 2026, scheduled for October 28 and 29 under the theme, “Partnership for Enduring Value: Building Resilient Supply Chains Beyond Mining.” The conference is expected to bring together suppliers, business operators and other stakeholders to discuss ways to strengthen local participation and build supply chains capable of meeting the operational demands of the mining industry. The involvement of almost 100 community vendors in Gold Fields’ supply chain provides an existing base from which further local enterprise development could take place. The country’s local-content framework provides a regulatory basis for increasing domestic participation in the mining supply chain. L.I. 2431 sets out requirements aimed at promoting Ghanaian participation in the supply of goods and services to the industry. The suppliers conference is expected to address procurement practices, opportunities for women-owned enterprises, environmental, social and governance considerations, safety and supply-chain disruptions. These issues reflect the need to balance reliable mining operations with broader expectations around local participation and responsible business practices. Disruptions in the supply of critical goods and services can affect production schedules and operating costs. A stronger domestic supplier base can provide additional sources of supply, while giving local businesses a greater stake in the industry’s performance. Gold Fields has also been involved in efforts to support small-scale mining formalisation in collaboration with the World Gold Council, as well as discussions around the potential relinquishment of part of the Tarkwa concession. The company’s wider community engagement includes development initiatives such as the Apinto Government Hospital project. These activities reflect different aspects of the relationship between mining operations and host communities, from economic participation and land access to social infrastructure. Procurement, however, offers a direct channel through which mining companies can engage domestic businesses and influence the distribution of economic opportunities. Gold Fields’ reported US$4.26 billion in-country expenditure and US$2.59 billion in host communities provide a measure of the economic activity associated with its operations.

items.title: South Africa evacuation: Minority rejects claims they coached returnees
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has denied allegations that it paid or attempted to coach some Ghanaian evacuees from South Africa to speak against the government over the handling of their repatriation and related allowances. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, said the Minority had neither paid nor persuaded any of the evacuees to make allegations against the government. His response follows a press conference held by some of the evacuees on Monday, October 26, during which they alleged that some opposition figures had attempted to coach them to speak against the government. Mr Jinapor rejected the claims, insisting that the Minority had not influenced any of the evacuees to speak publicly about the matter. “Let me place on record that at no point in time did the Minority engage, pay, and/or convince any of these people,” he said. He explained that some of the evacuees had decided to speak out after discovering discrepancies between the allowances they were reportedly entitled to receive and the amounts they actually received. The Minority has raised concerns about expenditure on the evacuation exercise, citing alleged duplicate entries, payment records without signatures, missing supporting receipts and claims by some evacuees that they did not receive the amounts recorded against their names. Mr Jinapor said these concerns remained unresolved despite explanations from the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. He therefore renewed the Minority’s call for an independent audit of the evacuation exercise to establish how the funds were spent and address the questions surrounding the payment records. The allegations about the evacuation expenditure and the claims that opposition figures attempted to coach evacuees remain disputed.

items.title: How Hubtel is rethinking AI in Ghana: Own your data, rent the intelligence
items.description: From the trader at Makola checking prices on her phone to the graduate in Kumasi searching for work, one question is getting louder across Ghana. Will artificial intelligence make life better, or will it take away what people already have? Ghana has placed its bet. In 2025, it launched a ten-year national AI strategy, and the government has committed $270 million to get the country ready. But for ordinary Ghanaians, the most useful answers may come from a local company that has already tried, stumbled, and found a smarter way forward. That company is Hubtel. Head of Engineering, Augustine Adjei, told the national audience during the premiere of the AI & Ghana documentary on Joy News exactly what Ghana’s AI journey looks like from the inside, and why the country does not need to start big to win. About the Digital Economy Forum The Digital Economy Forum is a national thought-leadership platform conceived by Hubtel to create evidence-based conversations about the technologies, policies and ideas shaping Ghana’s economic future. It combines original documentary storytelling with a televised debate on JoyNews and Joy FM, bringing together government, regulators, businesses, academics and everyday Ghanaians. The maiden edition tackled digital fraud and why trust matters in Ghana’s growing digital economy. The latest edition asked a bigger question: AI and the Ghana economy, opportunity or disruption? For Hubtel, which helps Ghanaians pay bills, send money and order goods, the stakes are personal. A digital economy only grows when people trust it, understand it and can benefit from it. The forum is Hubtel’s way of making sure that conversation happens in public, with the facts on the table and ordinary people in the room. Opportunity or disruption? Both, says Hubtel Asked whether AI is good or bad news for Ghana, Augustine Adjei refused to pick one side. “It is both,” he said. “Growth is hard and painful, but the disruption is a setback while the opportunity is exponential.” He compared it to a catapult. You get pulled back first, and that painful pull is what launches you forward. Change will hurt in places, but those who prepare will move faster than ever. When Hubtel tried to build its own AI Hubtel opened an AI lab in 2023, before chat apps like ChatGPT became part of everyday life. It hired skilled Ghanaian engineers to build AI from scratch. The lab’s biggest project helped the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) catch power theft. The system flagged meters that seemed not to be paying, traced back through the records and connected the dots. Hubtel also built its own fraud detection and call-centre tools. Then the world moved faster and cheaper. By 2025, global AI companies were selling far more powerful tools for about $20 to $25 a month. Hubtel did what any smart trader does when a better product appears at a lower price. It stopped trying to outbuild the giants and started buying access. Talent Isn’t the Problem Augustine Adjei explained the decision with a picture every Ghanaian understands. “Would you want an Italian chef to cook your fufu and light soup, or an equally competent Ghanaian chef who has lived here all their life?” he asked. The answer is obvious: the Ghanaian chef. But training that chef takes time and money. Until then, you hire the chef who can feed you today while you plan for tomorrow. He was clear that Ghana’s problem has never been brains. “Talent is equally distributed; resources are not,” he said. Hubtel had the people. What it did not have was the hundreds of millions of dollars global firms spend on AI. Own your data, rent the engine Hubtel did not just sign up for a free chatbot. It negotiated directly with leading global AI companies, which were surprised a Ghanaian firm could pay at that level. Under the deal, Hubtel runs the AI inside its own systems, keeps full ownership of its data, and the providers have promised not to use Hubtel’s information to train their models. Augustine Adjei summed up the rule simply: “Own what you can before you scale.” He also shared a funny but serious warning. When Hubtel tested a free AI model and asked it about the company, the model said Hubtel was headquartered in Kigali. AI only knows what you teach it, so Ghanaians must feed it Ghanaian facts. The best example of this thinking is Hubtel’s virtual call centre. Because so many Ghanaians transact on Hubtel every day, the phones ring constantly. An AI agent now answers first and can check a customer’s order status on the spot. It works because all the information it needs already belongs to Hubtel. It is built in Ghana, trained on Ghanaian data and speaks to customers in a Ghanaian accent. For Augustine Adjei, that is the point. “AI is not a thing, it is us. There is no AI without humans,” he said. “If we are biased, AI will be biased.” Honorable Sam George backs the Hubtel approach Communications Minister of Ghana, Honorable Sam George said Hubtel’s story shows why Ghana must fix its data first. “AI models are only as good as their data sets,” he said. Hubtel had found no simple way for companies in Ghana to share data. The Minister said government is building a national data exchange hub to connect about 48 public registries, from the Ghana Health Service to the National Identification Authority, so developers make one request instead of 48. Companies are welcome to join, as long as they contribute data too. On jobs, he echoed Hubtel’s message that people must grow with the technology. “Those who evolve and adapt will survive,” he said. “Those who fail to evolve and adapt will fall off.” Bright Simmons of Imani Africa, the night’s toughest critic of government spending, held up Hubtel as an example of doing AI in the right order: use a proven global tool first, then build local. “If you don’t define your problem extremely well, AI can’t give you answers,” he warned, adding: “We should not stay on the surface.” Five lessons for every Ghanaian You do not need to be a tech company to learn from Hubtel. Whether you run a chop bar, a boutique or a small office, the same rules apply: Start with what you already have. Your customer list, your records and the way you work are your biggest AI asset. Use what works today. Global AI tools are cheap and powerful, so use them while local options grow. Guard your information. Keep control of your data and know where it goes. Teach the AI about Ghana. If a tool thinks Hubtel is in Kigali, it can get your business wrong too. Think before you upload. Augustine Adjei said his phone holds his 74-year-old mother’s medical record, and he would not run it through a public chatbot without protection. Ghana’s AI future will not be decided by one big announcement. It will be shaped by businesses and individuals who test, learn, adjust and keep going. Hubtel has shown a practical path for the whole country: own your data, rent the engine, solve real problems for real customers and keep your people learning. Through the Digital Economy Forum, it is making sure every Ghanaian gets to hear that conversation.

Le vote intervient après la présentation des projets des quatre candidats devant les membres statutaires, chacun ayant eu l’occasion de défendre son programme et de convaincre les électeurs. items.title: Reps move to tighten rules for EV, CNG vehicle imports, demand local service centres
items.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stricter regulations on the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and related equipment, proposing mandatory local maintenance centres, genuine spare parts and after-sales support for importers. The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing framework for companies importing alternative-fuel vehicles, warning against the risk of Nigeria becoming a dumping ground for vehicles without adequate technical support and safety safeguards. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye during Wednesday’s plenary, where lawmakers raised concerns over consumer protection, vehicle safety, local investment and the country’s readiness for the growing adoption of cleaner transportation technologies. Under the proposed framework, the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies, would develop clear criteria for approving importers. Companies seeking approval could be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technicians. Other proposed conditions include investment in electric-vehicle charging stations or CNG refuelling facilities, compliance with national safety and environmental standards, and submission of consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The House also proposed a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and protect consumers. It stressed that the licensing process should be open, competitive and non-discriminatory, allowing all companies that meet the prescribed requirements to obtain approval. The lawmakers further called for tax incentives, import duty concessions and other fiscal benefits to be tied to compliance with the proposed framework to encourage investment in local infrastructure and technical capacity. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Dominic Okafor warned against allowing Nigeria to become a dumping ground for vehicles manufactured without adequate consideration for the needs of developing countries. He said importers must demonstrate their capacity to maintain the vehicles they bring into the country and provide adequate support to consumers after purchase. “It’s very important to see that all the players in this motion are dressed seriously, so that Nigeria is not made a dumping ground,” Okafor said. He observed that some manufacturers produce different categories of vehicles for Western markets and developing countries, including Nigeria, stressing the need for safeguards to ensure that imported vehicles meet local requirements. Okafor said electric vehicles required sustained technical support, access to spare parts and maintenance facilities, unlike products consumed immediately after purchase. “Electric vehicles are not a one-sell product,” he said, adding that the absence of maintenance centres could leave consumers stranded and expose them to avoidable costs. The lawmaker also raised safety concerns over CNG-powered vehicles and trucks, arguing that companies should not be permitted to import them commercially without adequate facilities and technical safeguards. “Efforts should be made that whoever that importer is issued to has some of these facilities, not just in it as a trading activity,” he added. Similarly, Rep. Kalejaiye Adeboye Paul supported the proposal, saying local maintenance and repair facilities were essential to sustaining Nigeria’s transition to alternative-fuel transportation. He noted that state governments were increasingly embracing the programme, making it necessary to prepare for the long-term implications of importing vehicles without building domestic technical capacity. “But I think that establishing their own centre here in Nigeria for maintenance and repairs is very essential. It has to be a condition for which we can continue to embrace this,” Paul said. He warned that Nigeria’s limited capacity to manufacture or assemble the vehicles could create challenges as adoption increased. “We are not manufacturing here. We are not assembling here. And we do not have what it takes to keep this going,” he said. He warned that Nigeria’s limited capacity to manufacture or assemble the vehicles could create challenges as adoption increased. “We are not manufacturing here. We are not assembling here. And we do not have what it takes to keep this going,” he said. Paul added that the consequences of operating the vehicles without adequate maintenance infrastructure might become more evident over time, urging lawmakers to support the proposed safeguards in the interest of consumers and the country. Rep. Stanley Olajide described the motion as timely, citing global concerns over greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. He said a properly regulated transition to cleaner transportation would enable Nigeria to contribute to environmental protection while advancing its development priorities. “I believe having this framework will not only be responsible as a nation, it will also help us toward the line of having an environment-friendly system where we can actually say we are contributing to the right cause in the world,” Olajide said. Rep. Sada Soli also backed the proposal, arguing that a clear legal framework was needed to support the Federal Government’s clean transportation policy. Soli recalled that the government had announced fiscal incentives for CNG and certain categories of electric vehicles, saying legislation would help establish clear rules for implementing the policy. “What is lacking in this policy is the legal aspect of it,” he said, urging the sponsor to develop the proposal into a bill to provide a comprehensive legal framework for regulating the sector. Soli identified environmental protection, lower transportation costs and employment generation as potential benefits of a well-managed transition to alternative-fuel vehicles. He also argued that the adoption of new transportation technologies could create opportunities for jobs and income generation if supported by appropriate policies and infrastructure. The lawmaker urged the sponsor to take the proposal further, saying the National Assembly should play an active role in establishing the legal framework rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to the executive. “We should not surrender it to the government because the government has built on this policy,” Soli said. The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment and Legislative Compliance to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. Following the debate, Speaker Tajudeen Abbas said the motion had received support and encouraged the sponsor to provide additional details on how the proposed policy would operate. items.title: Building inflation increases to 5.1% in September 2026, but cement inflation stood at -6.1%
items.description: The year-on-year inflation rate of the Prime Building Cost Index (PBCI) was 5.1% in September 2026, up from 4.6% in August 2026. The monthly change rate for September 2026 was 0.03%. According to the Ghana Statistical Service, building inflation remains low, despite an increase in September 2026. The drivers of the September inflation were plant and equipment costs that went up 19.1% over the year. At the group level, the Labour group inflation rate recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of -3.2% in September 2026, down from -2.9% in August 2026. The Material group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 6.5% in September 2026, up from 5.8% in August 2026, while the Plant group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 19.1%, up from 17.9% in August 2026. At the sub-group level, Reinforcement recorded the highest year-on-year inflation rate of 29.0%, while the sub-group Steel recorded the lowest year-on-year inflation rate of -8.8%. Fourteen sub-groups out of the 23 sub-groups recorded inflation rates above the national average of 5.1%. The year-on-year inflation halved over the year but has risen since March 2026. What the September figures mean to households For households, structural inputs cost less than a year ago, as cement inflation stood at −6.1% and steel −8.8%. Finishing and installation inputs, however, cost more, with plumbing +27.5%, glazing +20.6%, and tiles +9.2%. The overall building costs are 5.1% higher than in September 2025.

items.title: Bilawal calls for 'full stop' on conversations about new provinces
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Tuesday called for a “full stop” to conversations regarding the creation of new provinces. He made the remarks while speaking to the media at Spencer Eye Hospital in Karachi’s Lyari alongside Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah. Reiterating his party’s stance in response to a question over “pressure” the PPP was facing regarding the creation of new administrative units and the possibility of rolling back the 18th Amendment, Bilawal said the people of Sindh and their elected representatives had presented their decision and “now we should put a full stop to this conversation”. He said the Sindh Assembly had also made its stance in the matter evident for “at least seven to eight times now”. “The people here can determine the fate of this province and the city,” Bilawal asserted. “I think we should close this topic because the people themselves have closed it,” he said. When asked about ongoing conversations regarding a 28th constitutional amendment and whether the government had spoken to him in this regard, Bilawal simply replied: “No.” The PPP chairman was also questioned about the recent dispute between the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) and Pakistan Railways and the federal government’s lack of interest in the city. “The federal government should definitely pay attention to this city. Karachi is the country’s economic hub. Everyone else should pay attention to it,” he said. Bilawal’s remarks come amid an ongoing debate across the country about the creation of new administrative units, sparked by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s proposal for a dialogue among all political parties to bring about reforms to the current governance system and call for new provinces and urgent administrative reforms in July. At the time, the PPP had referred the question to its top decision-making forum, while the Sindh chief minister flatly rejected it; Lahore’s lawyers also called it unconstitutional and Sindhi nationalist groups have been demanding the minister’s resignation. However, since Naqvi’s remarks, various political parties have also spoken in favour of it and called for the creation of more provinces or administrative units for better governance. The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) — an ally of the PML-N-led ruling coalition — has been demanding that Karachi be designated a province separate from Sindh. However, the PPP, which rules Sindh and is also an ally of the PML-N government at the Centre along with MQM-P, has strongly opposed the suggested move. In September, the Sindh Assembly adopted a resolution rejecting all attempts to divide the province or create new administrative units , with the CM Murad declaring that “there will be no compromise on Sindh’s geographical unity”.

items.title: Kane, l’or de la patience (Par Cheikh Gora DIOP)
items.description: Il aura fallu attendre ses 33 ans. Lundi soir, au Palladium de Londres, Harry Kane a enfin soulevé le Ballon d’Or. La salle a scandé son prénom comme si elle réparait une longue injustice. Pour l’attaquant anglais, ce sacre vient couronner des années de travail, de buts et de désillusions. Longtemps, il a marqué sans gagner. Cette fois, il a les deux. Cinquième Anglais à recevoir le trophée après Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan et Michael Owen, Kane met fin à vingt-cinq ans d’attente pour son pays. Il succède aussi à Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, dernier joueur du Bayern Munich sacré, en 1981. Mais au-delà de ces repères historiques, c’est surtout le parcours d’un attaquant qui a fini par trouver la récompense à la hauteur de ses efforts qu’il faut retenir. À Tottenham, Kane avait beau empiler les buts, les trophées lui échappaient. Son départ pour Munich a changé la donne. Cette saison, il a inscrit 73 buts toutes compétitions confondues, dont 61 en 51 matches avec le Bayern. Avec 36 réalisations en Bundesliga, il a décroché le Soulier d’or européen. Sept passes décisives, un titre de champion d’Allemagne et une Coupe d’Allemagne complètent son bilan en club. Avec l’Angleterre, il a ajouté douze buts, dont six lors de la Coupe du monde. Difficile de faire plus convaincant. Surtout, Kane est devenu bien plus qu’un finisseur. Il décroche, sert ses partenaires, libère des espaces et participe au pressing. Il sait toujours conclure, mais il sait aussi faire jouer les autres. Son évolution n’a rien d’un miracle : elle récompense un travail patient et une volonté constante de progresser. L’instinct lui a donné les buts ; le travail a élargi son jeu. L’an dernier, il n’était que treizième du Ballon d’Or. Le voilà au sommet. Comme quoi, dans un football qui s’emballe pour les prodiges, il n’est pas nécessaire d’avoir tout gagné à 25 ans. À 33 ans, Kane vient rappeler que le talent peut mûrir longtemps et que la persévérance finit parfois par payer. Son sacre ne doit pourtant pas faire oublier ceux qui le suivent. Kylian Mbappé termine deuxième, tandis que Lamine Yamal, troisième et lauréat du Trophée Kopa, confirme qu’il faudra compter avec lui pendant de longues années. Le Français a déjà accumulé les buts et les records. L’Espagnol, à seulement 19 ans, possède encore le temps de transformer son immense potentiel en règne durable. Ils peuvent nourrir quelques regrets, mais certainement pas baisser les bras. Mbappé devra continuer à convertir ses exploits individuels en grands titres collectifs. Yamal, lui, devra garder cette audace et cette maturité sans brûler les étapes. Le Ballon d’Or leur échappe cette fois ; rien ne dit qu’il leur échappera toujours. Dans le football, les occasions reviennent à ceux qui savent les saisir. Les votants ont choisi Kane pour sa régularité, son efficacité et la force de sa saison. Pas besoin d’en faire trop pour convaincre : l’Anglais parle avec ses performances. Discret, travailleur, obstiné, il rappelle que le métier se juge aussi dans la durée, loin du clinquant et des promesses. On ne va pas s’en plaindre. Harry Kane est un beau vainqueur. Il n’a rien volé à personne. Il a attendu, travaillé et insisté, sans renoncer à ce qui fait sa force. Son sacre est aussi un message pour les jeunes talents : tout ne se joue pas à 18 ans, et une carrière ne se résume pas à une course contre le temps. Pour le natif de Londres, le Ballon d’Or a longtemps été un horizon lointain. Il est désormais entre ses mains. Quinze ans d’attente, une saison exceptionnelle et une soirée pour entrer dans l’histoire. cheikhgora.diop@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Niger : Niamey dénonce une frappe meurtrière menée depuis le Tchad
items.description: Le gouvernement nigérien a dénoncé lundi, une frappe aérienne menée par drone depuis le territoire tchadien, avec l’appui de la France, le samedi 24 octobre 2026, à Emilulu, dans la région d’Agadez. L’information a été rendue publique dans un communiqué lu à la télévision nationale, dans la soirée du lundi 26 octobre 2026. Selon le communiqué, cette frappe aurait fait deux (02) morts parmi les civils, plusieurs blessés et causé des dégâts matériels, notamment sur des véhicules. Le gouvernement nigérien accuse le Tchad de s’être engagé, depuis plusieurs mois, dans une démarche hostile à l’égard du Niger, en offrant une « profondeur stratégique » à des mercenaires qui s’attaqueraient aux populations ainsi qu’aux infrastructures stratégiques et énergétiques du pays. Face à cette situation, Niamey condamne fermement cet acte, qu’il qualifie d’agression et considère comme une violation flagrante de sa souveraineté nationale, de l’article 2, paragraphe 4, de la Charte des Nations unies et des principes fondateurs de l’Union africaine. Dans son communiqué, le gouvernement nigérien annonce plusieurs mesures, notamment une protestation officielle par voie diplomatique, tout en appelant N’Djamena à mettre fin à toute manœuvre hostile à son égard. Niamey prévoit également de saisir le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies ainsi que le Conseil de paix et de sécurité de l’Union africaine. Le gouvernement nigérien affirme enfin se réserver le droit de prendre « toutes les mesures nécessaires » pour défendre sa souveraineté, sa population et ses intérêts. Il appelle par ailleurs la communauté internationale à prendre acte de la situation. Minute.bf

Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty AK-47 magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number (NIN) document belonging to one Mr Umar Yusuf, and the sum of ₦20 The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Kolo Gara, commended the troops for their vigilance, proactive response and successful recovery of the items. items.title: Reines d’or (par Ndiol Maka SECK)
items.description: Le masque en or de la dame Ngoye Fall avait déjà fait couler beaucoup d’encre et de salive au Sénégal. En 2025, c’était au tour de l’influenceuse Mame Ndiaye Savon de faire parler d’elle en exhibant d’impressionnantes quantités d’or pour marquer son entrée dans le cercle très fermé des « diriyanké », ces femmes de grande classe. Oumou Sininta, du Mali, elle, a placé la barre encore plus haut. À l’occasion d’une cérémonie de mariage, la dame se serait retrouvée couverte d’or de la tête aux pieds. Dix kilogrammes de métal précieux, selon la presse people. L’image, elle, a fait le tour des réseaux sociaux : éblouissante pour les uns, choquante pour les autres. Soyons clairs : posséder de l’or n’a rien de condamnable. Pour beaucoup de femmes, ces bijoux représentent bien plus qu’un simple accessoire de beauté. Ils sont un patrimoine, une assurance contre les lendemains incertains. Mais entre porter de l’or pour se faire belle et en porter au point de transformer son cou en support de coffre-fort, il y a peut-être une limite à ne pas franchir. Oumou Sininta a illuminé sa cérémonie de mariage. Reste à espérer que sa lune de miel ne se transforme pas en séance prolongée chez le kinésithérapeute. ndiolmaka.seck@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Violences du 17 octobre en France : une «taxe émeutes» sur les contrats d’assurance dans les tuyaux
items.description: Les cotisations d'assurance de tous les Francais risquent d'augmenter l'annee prochaine. Sur fond de pillages du 17 octobre, la creation d'un regime emeutes ferait son chemin en France. a en croire Les echos , qui affirme avoir mis la main sur des documents provisoires , « deux projets de decrets et deux projets d'arretes ont ete presentes mi-octobre au comite consultatif de la legislation et de la reglementation financieres (CCLRF) ». La loi de finances pour 2026 a cree la « garantie emeutes », apres les milliards d'euros de degâts occasionnes aux collectivites et aux entreprises lors d'emeutes telles que celles observees en Nouvelle-Caledonie en 2024, ou apres celles declenchees par la mort de Nahel en 2023. Les parlementaires prennent egalement en compte les degâts et les pertes occasionnes aux entreprises lors de la revolte des Gilets jaunes . Le deblocage de ce fonds de mutualisation, au profit des assureurs pour le dedommagement de leurs assures, doit faire l'objet d'une commission statuant sur la nature de ces emeutes. La « taxe attentat » augmentera egalement de deux euros Une « cotisation de solidarite » de 0,8 %, prelevee sur les contrats d'assurance dommages (habitation, automobile, entreprises, etc.), permettrait d'alimenter ce fonds a hauteur de 400 millions d'euros par an. Un mecanisme qui n'est pas sans rappeler la « taxe attentat », qui alimente le fonds de garantie des victimes de terrorisme et contribue egalement a l'indemnisation des victimes d'infractions de droit commun (agressions, homicides, viols, violences conjugales, etc.). Cette contribution devrait elle aussi augmenter de deux euros par contrat automobile et habitation debut 2027. Le dispositif de garantie contre les emeutes n'est toutefois pas encore entre en vigueur. « Son application reste notamment suspendue a une decision de la Commission europeenne sur sa conformite au droit de l'Union », soulignait le Journal du dimanche (JDD) au debut du mois.

items.title: Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him
items.description: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. China’s foreign ministry said it was aware of the reports regarding Mbappe, who on Monday finished runner-up to English forward Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or award for the world’s best player. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and removed all advertisements involving Mbappe. On the CCTV website, La Liga matches this weekend were still on its online viewing schedule. – Drawing China’s ire – Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based sports consultancy firm Key-Solution Sports Consulting, speaking before Mbappe apologised, said a rapid response was needed to quell the growing crisis. “It’s crucial to make a sincere statement. The sooner, the better,” Zhang told AFP. Fans made their feelings clear. “I used to really enjoy watching Mbappe play on the pitch,” Zhang Jingqi, 30, who works at a mall in Beijing, said. “But ever since this news broke yesterday I have lost that admiration, sorry to say.” AFP The post Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’Ukraine demande à cinq pays européens de lui céder 10 % de leurs stocks de missiles antiaériens
items.description: L'Ukraine a demande a l'Allemagne, au Royaume-Uni, a la France, a la Pologne et a l'Italie d'envisager le transfert de 10 % de leurs stocks de missiles intercepteurs, notamment pour les systemes de defense antiaerienne Patriot et IRIS-T. Cette demande a ete formulee par le ministre ukrainien de la Defense, Evgueni Khmara, aupres des pays du groupe E5, selon un communique publie le 26 octobre par son ministere. Pour obtenir ces missiles sans attendre les prochaines livraisons, Kiev propose un mecanisme d'echange. Les cinq pays sollicites seraient invites a puiser dans leurs propres reserves, en contrepartie de missiles destines a l'Ukraine dans le cadre de contrats deja conclus et finances par un credit de l'Union europeenne. « La premiere priorite critique est la defense antiaerienne », a declare Evgueni Khmara dans un message publie sur Telegram le 27 octobre. Le ministre sollicite egalement le financement de nouveaux achats de systemes portables de defense antiaerienne, ainsi que leur transfert depuis les stocks occidentaux. Ces equipements sont notamment destines a lutter contre les drones a reaction. Les autorites ukrainiennes reconnaissent une situation critique Cette demande intervient alors que Kiev reconnaît des difficultes importantes dans sa defense antiaerienne. Volodymyr Zelensky a precedemment admis que le manque de missiles empechait les forces ukrainiennes d'intercepter les cibles balistiques. Egor Tchernev, president de la commission parlementaire chargee de la securite nationale, de la defense et du renseignement, a quant a lui decrit la situation comme la plus difficile depuis le debut du conflit. Les approvisionnements americains font egalement l'objet de tensions. Zelensky affirme attendre depuis pres d'un mois l'approbation du chef du Pentagone, Pete Hegseth, pour l'envoi de missiles destines aux systemes Patriot et NASAMS. Moscou estime que les livraisons occidentales prolongent le conflit Les cinq pays du groupe E5 preparent parallelement de nouveaux programmes d'assistance militaire a l'Ukraine pour l'hiver. Le ministre allemand de la Defense, Boris Pistorius, a confirme la preparation de ces aides apres une reunion avec ses homologues a Paris. Les informations communiquees ne font toutefois etat d'aucun engagement precis concernant la demande de transfert de 10 % des stocks de missiles. Moscou denonce depuis longtemps la poursuite des livraisons d'armes occidentales a Kiev, qu'elle considere comme un obstacle au reglement du conflit. Le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a reaffirme que cette assistance militaire ne favorisait pas les negociations et ne pourrait empecher la Russie de poursuivre ses objectifs militaires. Selon Peskov, un reglement du conflit pourrait intervenir plus rapidement si les pays occidentaux mettaient fin a leurs livraisons d'armements a l'Ukraine.

items.title: ‎US partners with FG to end hunger, starvation
items.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA – THE Federal Government has received a major boost in its fight against hunger and child malnutrition, with the United States-backed Operation End Starvation (OES) seeking a direct partnership with the Federal Government to help scale up life-saving nutrition interventions across the country. ‎‎The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this in Abuja when he led a delegation from OES and agencies under the Health Ministry to seek collaboration with the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. ‎‎The proposed alliance is expected to strengthen Nigeria’s response to acute child malnutrition, with particular attention to vulnerable children, pregnant women and lactating mothers. ‎‎OES Chief Executive Officer, Williams Holdsworth Moore, said the organisation was impressed by Nigeria’s commitment and the capacity of its health leadership, describing the country as a priority site for its global intervention. ‎‎“We have met with the Nigerian health team, and they are one of the best of many we have met,” Moore said. ‎‎He explained that OES, supported by a macro grant from the United States Government and global philanthropists, plans to channel more than one billion dollars annually towards preventing child deaths caused by starvation. ‎‎“We want to move one billion dollars to end starvation in the next two years across Sub-Saharan Africa. The burden is high, but the capacity is also very high,” he said. ‎‎Moore added that the U.S. State Department had approved Nigeria as part of the organisation’s priority outlook, adding that OES wanted to demonstrate successful large-scale investment through direct government partnership within the next two years. ‎‎He explained thatOperation End Starvation, an initiative of the Eleanor Crook Foundation, is a public-private nonprofit focused on ending child malnutrition and starvation-related deaths across Sub-Saharan Africa, including Nigeria. ‎‎Prof. Pate said Nigeria was already implementing strong frameworks to confront malnutrition, citing the National Community Food Bank Programme, which is being delivered in partnership with the Office of the First Lady. ‎‎He said the programme, recently rolled out across the six geopolitical zones, was already recording positive impact and would be expanded to reach more vulnerable households. ‎‎“Nigeria is working hard to scale down its 6.4 million figure of acute child malnutrition, while also attending to the health of pregnant women and lactating mothers,” Pate said. ‎‎“A lot of good things are already happening in the country.” ‎‎The National Community Food Bank Programme is designed to provide nutritious, locally sourced food to children under six, pregnant women, lactating mothers and other high-risk households through community food banks linked to primary healthcare centres. ‎‎The First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu welcomed the delegation and commended the quality of expertise and commitment within Nigeria’s public institutions, saying the country’s health team would justify any support received. ‎‎“It has been a delight working with Prof. Pate, Dr Muyi and others. I also work with the Ministry of Education and others. The manpower we have now in the ministries is so wonderful,” she said. ‎‎The First Lady assured the OES delegation that resources provided through the partnership would be deployed transparently and effectively. ‎‎“I assure you that whatever aid you give us, this health team would put it to good use,” she said. ‎‎She said Nigeria deserved better and that the reforms being undertaken by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu were gradually restoring the country’s systems. ‎‎“Nigeria deserves better, and there is nothing we give to her that is too much because if the system works, it will ultimately come back to us,” the First Lady said. ‎ ‎ The post ‎US partners with FG to end hunger, starvation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: LFR 2026 : le texte renvoyé en commission pour de nouvelles discussions
items.description: Le projet de Loi de finances rectificative (Lfr) 2026 est renvoyé en commission des finances et du contrôle budgétaire. À l’ouverture de la discussion générale, mardi, le ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, Cheikh Diba, a sollicité cette mesure afin de permettre au gouvernement et aux députés de poursuivre leurs échanges. Pour justifier sa demande, le ministre a invoqué l’article 84 du règlement intérieur de l’Assemblée nationale, qui prévoit le renvoi d’un texte devant la commission saisie au fond au cours de la discussion générale, jusqu’à la clôture de celle-ci. « Le gouvernement sollicite ce renvoi en commission des finances et du contrôle budgétaire pour des discussions complémentaires dans les plus brefs délais possibles », a déclaré Cheikh Diba. Cette démarche intervient dans un contexte de tensions autour de l’examen du texte budgétaire. Le ministre a notamment évoqué les échanges engagés lundi 26 octobre, à la suite de l’appel au dialogue du Premier ministre, ainsi que les correspondances échangées entre le président de la commission des finances et le ministère. Le retour en commission doit permettre d’approfondir l’examen des préoccupations soulevées par les députés et d’explorer les possibilités de compromis. Le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Ousmane Sonko, a pris acte de la demande du gouvernement et a immédiatement convoqué la Conférence des présidents. S.G

items.title: Two charged with security offences over plot at UK airbase used by US
items.description: UK anti-terrorism police said on Tuesday that two men have been charged with national security offences after an incident last month at a British airbase used by the United States, linking the scare to Iran. The head of National Counter Terrorism Policing, Laurence Taylor, said two British men aged 24 had been charged: one with assisting a foreign intelligence service, believed to be in Iran, and another with entering a prohibited place for a purpose “prejudicial” to the United Kingdom. This is the first time that anyone has been charged over the incident at RAF Fairford, after police arrested seven suspects in the days afterwards, before releasing them on bail. Police were called to the Royal Air Force’s Fairford base in southwest England in the early hours of Sept 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several white vans engaged in “suspicious” activity. “While some of the circumstances remain unclear , we are confident that this activity was conducted on behalf of a foreign intelligence service,” Taylor told reporters on Tuesday outside Metropolitan Police headquarters in London. Days after the incident, the US withdrew all its B-1 bombers from the base. Suspects charged A week ago police said they had re-arrested two of the suspects, one of whom has now been charged. Police charged 24-year-old Nouman Essghir with entering or approaching a “prohibited place” for a purpose “prejudicial” to the interests of the UK. Essghir was arrested at the scene in Gloucestershire and then released on bail, before police re-arrested him a week ago. The police chief said the charge against Essghir related to “suspected activity” more than a month earlier, on Saturday Aug 22, without giving any details. The second man who has been charged, 24-year-old Mohmed Ahmad Abdulkarim, was arrested after being interviewed under caution over the last week, police said. He has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service. “In this case, we believe that country to be Iran ,” the police said. Taylor said Counter Terrorism Policing had seen “a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state”. “This is not a theoretical threat. This is something we are responding to every day,” he added. Both of the charged men live in Westminster, a district in central London. Six other men remain on bail, one of them a dual UK-Iranian national who had been re-arrested last week. Taylor acknowledged that some of the police’s “decisions made during our investigations can sometimes appear illogical”. “But I want to make it very clear that there will always be a good reason or rationale behind them,” he said.

items.title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ licences over $8.38m debt
items.description: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mining leases and prospecting licences of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Ower Mines, citing more than US$8.38 million in unpaid fees and alleged breaches of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Commission said it followed the legally prescribed process after the company failed to settle outstanding Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees or remedy other breaches identified by the regulator. The company has instituted legal proceedings against the State to challenge the termination, according to the Commission. The Commission said Northern Ashanti Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010. Under Section 24 of Act 703 and the terms of its lease agreement, the company was required to pay annual mineral right fees. However, the Commission said the company had accumulated US$8.33 million in unpaid fees relating to its mining leases for the period from 2010 to 2025, alongside US$49,928 owed on prospecting licences covering 2019 to 2025. On April 14, 2025, the Commission issued Notices to Remedy Breach under Section 68(2) of Act 703 and Regulation 200(3) of the Minerals and Mining Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2176), requiring the company to settle the outstanding amounts. The Commission said the company failed to comply within the stipulated period. Beyond the unpaid fees, the Commission said its assessment found that Northern Ashanti Mines had not undertaken meaningful mining operations on the concession for more than two years. It said this constituted a breach of Section 69(1) of Act 703. According to the Commission, the company was given an opportunity to regularise its position but failed to remedy the identified breaches. The Commission said it notified the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources on April 7, 2026, requesting that a notice of termination be served on the company. The Minister approved the issuance of the notice on April 24, 2026, and the Commission proceeded with the termination process on April 30, 2026. It maintained that the decision was taken in accordance with the law and that due process had been followed at every stage. The Commission also rejected suggestions that the company’s status as an indigenous business should exempt it from statutory obligations. “Once granted, a holder must abide by the rules, whether they are an indigenous company or not, and this includes the payment of statutory fees and the undertaking of meaningful mining operations,” the Commission stated. The Commission said the terminated mineral rights had reverted to the State, without extinguishing liabilities the company incurred before the termination. It said it would pursue the recovery of the outstanding fees and take steps to protect the affected assets against encroachment and other unlawful activities. “The Commission reserves the right and shall pursue the company to pay all the sums it owes to the State,” the statement said. The Commission confirmed that Northern Ashanti Mines had initiated legal proceedings challenging the termination after acknowledging receipt of the notice. It criticised the company’s media campaign, arguing that its public statements risked undermining the judicial process while the dispute remained before the courts.

items.title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports
items.description: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session. The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. items.title: Une affaire de vie ou de mort (par Seydou KA)
items.description: Écrire est un acte grave. On peut même dire que c’est une affaire de vie ou de mort. L’écrivain canadien d’origine haïtienne Thélyson Orélien vient tragiquement d’en faire l’expérience. Cité comme le phénomène de la rentrée littéraire pour son roman « C’était ça ou mourir », il est brutalement tombé de haut. Accusé d’avoir utilisé l’IA pour écrire ce roman, l’écrivain de 38 ans s’était d’abord emmuré dans un silence assourdissant avant de reconnaître, à deux temps, être un faussaire. Il a reconnu le plagiat et d’avoir utilisé l'IA « dans le processus de création » pour des « recherches historiques ». Mais face à l’accumulation de preuves et la persistance du doute, il a fini par admettre que sa parole ne valait plus rien. Personnellement, j’espérais, jusqu’au dernier moment, que ce n’était qu’une énième cabale contre un écrivain noir, alimentée par la clameur des réseaux sociaux. Hélas. Mais personne ne devrait se réjouir de ce qui lui arrive, car la chute d’un homme n’est pas belle à voir. Lâché de toutes parts, le voilà condamné à une longue solitude pour le reste de sa vie. Pour lui, c’était donc ça (la célébrité, les prix littéraires et la richesse) ou la mort sociale. Malheureusement, le destin lui a cruellement choisi la seconde alternative. Avant lui, d’autres écrivains ont connu le même sort. Pour s’en limiter à un seul exemple, pensons au sort réservé au Malien Yambo Ouologuem, qui connût également un double ban : celui des siens, les tenants de la négritude dont il contrarie la narration sur l’Afrique ; et un deuxième, plus tardif, de ceux qui l’ont primé avant de l’accuser de plagiat. Comme le montre Elgas dans son essai intitulé « Les bons ressentiments : essai sur le malaise post-colonial » (Riveneuve, 2023, 219 p.), la littérature est le champ par excellence de l’accusation. Le roman francophone, dit-il, recèle de cadavres enfouis sous terre. D’autres écrivains n’ont pas été accusés de plagiat, mais de bien pire. Après la publication de son roman « Les Versets sataniques » en 1988, l’écrivain indo-britannico-américain Salman Rushdie a vécu plusieurs années sous protection policière après que l’ayatollah Rouhollah Khomeiny, guide suprême de l’Iran, ait émis une fatwa appelant à son assassinat. Le 12 août 2022, il est grièvement poignardé lors d’une conférence à Chautauqua dans l’État de New York, une attaque qui lui fait perdre l’usage d’un œil. Dans le monde chrétien, pendant des siècles, des milliers d’écrivains ont vu leurs livres interdits par le Vatican pour hérésie, immoralité ou critique du pouvoir. Sur cette liste d’écrivains « mis à l’index », on retrouve des noms célèbres comme Honoré de Balzac, Émile Zola, Jean-Paul Sartre, Stendhal, René Descartes, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Denis Diderot, Baruch Spinoza, etc. D’autres (Tolstoï, Martin Luther, Alberto Maravia) ont été purement excommuniés. Pour en revenir à l’affaire Thélyson Orélien, je suis d’accord avec lui lorsqu’il dit qu’on ne devrait jamais menacer de mort quelqu’un à cause de ses écrits. « Ce que je suis en train de vivre, c’est énorme, ça a dépassé le cadre littéraire, ça va trop loin », a alerté l'auteur. Pour autant, le plagiat reste un acte déshonorant, qui jette le discrédit sur son auteur et le ridiculise aux yeux du public. Pour les auteurs de l’Antiquité, les plagiaires étaient assimilés à des « voleurs d’enfants d’autrui ». À l’heure de l’IA, le phénomène a pris une dimension beaucoup plus inquiétante, posant même le débat sur l’avenir de la littérature. Le débat est loin d’être clos puisque là où d’autres traquent l’IA à coup de détecteurs qui parfois se contredisent, des entrepreneurs ont lancé, le 21 octobre dernier, un nouveau prix littéraire pour récompenser une œuvre coécrite avec l’IA. Baptisé prix Pascal, il est ouvert « à toute personne qui écrit en français, partout dans la francophonie, sans condition de nationalité ni de résidence, sans éditeur ». seydou.ka@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Renaissance Casa Anfa : Le Groupe Anfa Realties lance officiellement la commercialisation de son projet art déco au cœur de Casa Anfa
items.description: Inspirée d'une époque iconique, pensée pour une vie contemporaine, Renaissance ouvre sa commercialisation avec des studios et des appartements de deux et trois chambres, au sein d'une résidence pensée dans l'esprit Art Déco. Le groupe Anfa Realties annonce le lancement officiel de la commercialisation de Renaissance , son nouveau projet résidentiel situé dans le quartier de Casa Anfa, à Casablanca. Ce programme s'inscrit dans la continuité des réalisations du groupe, qui a livré près de 2 000 unités depuis sa création en 2006. Une architecture affirmée, inspirée de l'Art Déco Renaissance Casa Anfa puise son identité dans le vocabulaire architectural de l'Art Déco : façades blanches rythmées de balcons aux courbes généreuses et de ferronneries géométriques, dans une symétrie affirmée. Cette écriture, inspirée d'une époque iconique, est ici réinterprétée pour répondre aux exigences de la vie contemporaine : espaces optimisés, matériaux de haute qualité et prestations pensées pour le quotidien. Des espaces pensés pour l'art de vivre La résidence propose des studios, ainsi que des appartements de deux et trois chambres, pensés pour différents profils d'acquéreurs. Les futurs résidents bénéficieront d'un ensemble de prestations dédiées au bien-être : piscine, salle de sport et espaces extérieurs paysagers, dans un cadre sécurisé au cœur de l'un des quartiers en devenir de Casablanca. Une localisation stratégique, au cœur de Casa Anfa Renaissance Casa Anfa bénéficie d'un emplacement privilégié au sein de ce quartier en pleine transformation, appelé à devenir l'un des pôles résidentiels et d'affaires structurants de Casablanca. La résidence est mitoyenne de l'École Louis Massignon de Casa Anfa et se trouve à proximité immédiate du centre commercial Aeria Mall, offrant à ses futurs résidents un accès direct aux commerces, aux services et à une offre scolaire de premier plan, le tout à quelques minutes des grands axes de la ville. En choisissant d'y implanter Renaissance, le groupe Anfa Realties confirme son ambition de proposer des adresses à la fois architecturalement singulières et stratégiquement situées. « Avec Renaissance, nous voulions offrir à Casa Anfa une architecture qui ne se démode pas. L'Art Déco n'est pas ici un simple décor : c'est le fil conducteur de tout le projet, de la façade jusqu'aux espaces de vie. » – Anfa Realties The post Renaissance Casa Anfa : Le Groupe Anfa Realties lance officiellement la commercialisation de son projet art déco au cœur de Casa Anfa appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Burkina Faso : La Douane saisit 2 310 bâtons de dynamite et 7 500 détonateurs
items.description: La Direction générale des Douanes a présenté, ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, des produits explosifs saisis par ses services, dont 2 310 bâtons de dynamite et 7 500 détonateurs. Face à la persistance des pratiques de contrebande, le directeur général des Douanes, le Dr Yves Kafando, appelle les fraudeurs à y mettre fin et prévient que les contrevenants s’exposent à des sanctions renforcées. La lutte contre la fraude et la contrebande se poursuit au Burkina Faso. Les services douaniers ont réalisé deux saisies portant sur des produits explosifs susceptibles de représenter un danger pour les populations et l’environnement. 2 310 bâtons de dynamite ont été interceptés dans un camion de transit, tandis que 7 500 détonateurs ont été découverts dans un bus de transport de passagers. La présentation de ces produits a été l’occasion pour le directeur général des Douanes de rappeler les risques liés à leur circulation . « Ce matin, nous constatons la saisie de bâtons détonants et de détonateurs. Des produits très nocifs, non seulement parce qu’ils peuvent mettre en danger la vie des citoyens, mais également détruire l’environnement et les animaux » , a déclaré le Dr Yves Kafando. Au-delà de ces saisies, le responsable de l’administration douanière déplore la persistance des pratiques frauduleuses, malgré les appels répétés adressés aux acteurs concernés. Selon lui, certains continuent de recourir à des stratagèmes pour échapper aux contrôles des agents sur le terrain. « Depuis un certain temps, la dynamique a été enclenchée. Malgré cela, il y a toujours des récalcitrants, ceux-là qui pensent qu’ils peuvent toujours utiliser des stratagèmes pour contourner la vigilance des agents sur le terrain » , a-t-il fait savoir. « Ceux qui veulent tester le niveau de vigilance des agents paieront cela à leurs dépens », Dr Yves Kafando Le directeur général des Douanes affirme que les avertissements adressés aux faux importateurs et aux contrebandiers n’ont pas suffi à mettre un terme à ces pratiques. Il annonce ainsi un durcissement des mesures visant les personnes qui persistent dans ces activités, particulièrement lorsque celles-ci mettent en danger la vie des citoyens. « Nous avons passé le temps à appeler les faux importateurs, les contrebandiers à abandonner la pratique. Malheureusement, ça perdure. Ce sont donc des dispositions qui ont été inscrites pour punir davantage les récalcitrants », a indiqué le Dr Yves Kafando. Il a également évoqué le durcissement du cadre de lutte contre les pratiques de contrebande à l’Assemblée législative du peuple (ALP). Pour lui, la vigilance des agents douaniers et les mesures prises doivent contribuer à décourager ceux qui tentent de contourner les contrôles. « À ces récalcitrants, je les invite à abandonner. Aujourd’hui, ceux qui veulent tester le niveau de vigilance des agents paieront cela à leurs dépens. Ils sont littéralement engagés, très vigilants », a martelé le directeur général des Douanes. À travers ces opérations, l’administration douanière entend poursuivre la lutte contre la circulation illicite de produits dangereux et renforcer la protection des populations. Le Dr Yves Kafando réaffirme ainsi la détermination de ses services à maintenir la pression sur les réseaux de fraude et de contrebande au Burkina Faso.
